quote: Recordings were made at 20, 40, 60 and in Group III also at 90 min after needle insertion or intradermal injection.
proposed_wording: Searches of Europe PMC and of an earlier worker's PubMed searches through October 2026 found no study reporting a skin blood flow reading from a local anaesthetic wheal free of the puncture response; the needle-only and saline arms of Cederholm 1991 (PMID 2038927) allow the drug effect to be separated only by contrast, and the puncture response alone has been quantified independently by laser Doppler (Holloway 1980, PMID 7351489).
reason: Nothing found measures a wheal's drug effect without a puncture, which is a design necessity rather than a gap anyone could close. Cederholm 1991 does carry needle-only and saline arms, so a drug-minus-saline contrast exists and the sentence would be more exact as 'no reading uncontaminated by the puncture response' rather than 'no clean drug-only reading'. The page's own convention at 0.1 already scopes its negatives as search-limited, so the correction needed is to the wording, not to the page's position.

records_read.citation: Sjoberg M, Karlsson PA, Nordborg C, Wallgren A, Nitescu P, Appelgren L, Linder LE, Curelaru I. Neuropathologic findings after long-term intrathecal infusion of morphine and bupivacaine mixtures for pain treatment in cancer patients. Anesthesiology 1992;76:173-186
records_read.matches: A human measurement of what prolonged local-anaesthetic exposure does to nerve tissue: 15 patients, 4 to 274 days of intrathecal bupivacaine-containing infusion, with neuropathological examination of meninges, nerve roots and spinal cord recorded alongside clinical neurological deficits.
records_read.misses: Spinal nerve roots and cord, not cutaneous small fibres, and no fibre-density count; the infusate was a mixture with morphine and preservatives and most patients had prior radiotherapy, antineoplastics or pre-existing deficits.

quote: The pathologic findings of the spinal column, the meninges, the nerve roots, and the spinal cord, and the clinical neurologic deficits were recorded in 15 patients (5 men and 10 women), aged 26-83 (median 68) yr, treated for 4-274 (median 81) days with intrathecal infusions of morphine (with preservatives [sodium metabisulfite and sodium edetate]) and bupivacaine mixtures, given through open, subcutaneously tunneled nylon catheters.
proposed_wording: Wehrfritz 2011 (PMID 21530339) appears to be the only human study measuring epidermal nerve fibre density after prolonged local-anaesthetic exposure; a separate human study records neuropathological findings in nerve roots and spinal cord after months of intrathecal bupivacaine-containing infusion (Sjoberg 1992, PMID 1736693).
reason: Within the claim's recorded outcome - epidermal nerve fibre density - searches found no second human study, so the core of the claim holds. It is too broad as 'the only measurement in humans of what prolonged local-anaesthetic exposure does to the fibres at issue', because Sjoberg 1992 is a human study of months-long local-anaesthetic exposure with a nerve-tissue histological endpoint, in nerve roots rather than cutaneous small fibres and with morphine, preservatives and prior oncological treatment confounding it. Adding 'to cutaneous small fibres' or 'to epidermal nerve fibre density' makes the sentence exact.

records_read.matches: The nearest second study by design: double-blind, 20 human volunteers, intradermal, mixtures against a single agent, duration of intradermal anaesthesia as the endpoint.

proposed_wording: Not found in searches of Europe PMC and Amass BiomedCore, and of an earlier worker's PubMed searches, through October 2026: no second study measuring an ester-plus-amide local-anaesthetic mixture by the intradermal route in humans with a duration endpoint. The nearest second study mixes two amides intradermally in volunteers (PMID 6751499); the same ester-plus-amide pair has been studied in isolated rat sciatic nerve (PMID 7191228).
reason: A Europe PMC title/abstract search combining mixture terms, intradermal terms, duration and ester-agent names returned exactly one record, Kim 1979 itself; two broader topic searches and two reused PubMed searches turned up no other human intradermal ester-plus-amide mixture study. Everything adjacent fails one element: PMID 6751499 is amide-plus-amide, PMID 7191228 is an isolated nerve, PMID 11091131 is a mouse with unmixed agents. The page's convention at 0.1 already scopes this as search-limited, which is the right framing to keep.
